heroHeadline: Junta Drones Kill 9 in Ngazun, Mandalay — Including Mother Shielding Infant; Min Aung Hlaing Announces India State Visit — Day 1,943
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,943 of Myanmar's civil war (May 29, 2026), SAC armed drone strikes killed nine civilians in Ngazun Township, Mandalay Region — including a woman who died shielding an infant — following a brief resistance clash, continuing the junta's documented pattern of collective punishment against civilian populations in PDF-active zones. In a simultaneous diplomatic development, Myanmar junta-installed President Min Aung Hlaing announced his first state visit to India (May 30–June 3, 2026): bilateral talks with PM Modi in New Delhi on June 1, covering strategic, economic, and connectivity cooperation, marking the highest-level India-Myanmar engagement since the coup. The visit deepens India's engagement with the junta despite its scorched-earth offensive in Chin State (40,000+ displaced) and the ongoing five-front war. The Myawaddy–Mae Sot Friendship Bridge No. 2, closed since August 2025 due to conflict, quietly reopened on May 28 for limited twice-daily truck traffic — a signal of junta consolidation of the Karen border trade corridor after the SAC's May 19 recapture of Maw Taung. The junta's multi-front May 2026 offensive remains acute across Rakhine (AA advance on Kyaukphyu Chinese port), Kachin (KIA guerrilla ambushes despite 300-vehicle SAC reinforcement), Sagaing (internal resistance dispute over gold mining rights), Karen, and Chin State simultaneously. UN documents 16.2 million Burmese requiring humanitarian aid — nearly one-third of the population.
